30640-anything-once.title: Anything Once
30640-anything-once.creator: Unknown
30640-anything-once.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Had she realized that those same worn, faded garments bore the stamp of one of New York's most exclusive tailors! that the boots were London-made, and the golf-stockings which met the corduroy knickerbockers came from one of Scotland's famous mills, it would have meant just exactly nothing in her young life.

58784-and-gone-tomorrow.title: And Gone Tomorrow
58784-and-gone-tomorrow.creator: Unknown
58784-and-gone-tomorrow.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The fellow wasn't kidding him. He was serious enough. But a couple of minutes ago it had been May 15, 1954. He looked at his watch and grunted. Less than four minutes ago it had been 1954. Now it was June 3, 2054. There were four steel walls. There was a steel chair. There were no windows.

arxiv-1806-06072.title: Bootstrapping two-loop Feynman integrals for planar 𝒩 = 𝟒 \mathbf{\mathcal{N}=4} sYM Preprint: MPP-2018-135, MITP/18-049
arxiv-1806-06072.creator: ​​​ Johannes Henn, ​​​, Enrico Herrmann, ​​​, Julio Parra-Martinez
arxiv-1806-06072.description: Abstract We derive analytic results for the symbol of certain two-loop Feynman integrals relevant for seven- and eight-point two-loop scattering amplitudes in planar 𝒩 = 4 \mathcal{N}=4 super-Yang–Mills theory. We use a bootstrap inspired strategy, combined with a set of second-order partial differential equations that provide powerful constraints on the symbol ansatz.

arxiv-2110-04853.title: Manifest colour-kinematics duality and double-copy in the string-based formalism Journal: .
arxiv-2110-04853.creator: Naser Ahmadiniaz, Filippo Maria Balli, Olindo Corradini, Cristhiam Lopez-Arcos, Alexander Quintero Vélez, Christian Schubert
arxiv-2110-04853.description: Abstract The relation for the gravity polarisation tensor as the tensor product of two gluon polarisation vectors has been well-known for a long time, but a version of this relation for multi-particle fields is presently still not known. Here we show that in order for this to happen we first have to ensure that the multi-particle polarisations satisfy colour-kinematics duality.

arxiv-2111-02560.title: Geometry unites synchrony, chimeras, and waves in nonlinear oscillator networks
arxiv-2111-02560.creator: Roberto C. Budzinski, Tung T. Nguyen, Jacqueline Đoàn, Ján Mináč, Terrence J. Sejnowski, Lyle E. Muller
arxiv-2111-02560.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Roberto C. Budzinski, Tung T. Nguyen, Jacqueline Đoàn, Ján Mináč, Terrence J. Sejnowski, Lyle E. Muller. One of the simplest mathematical models in the study of nonlinear systems is the Kuramoto model, which describes synchronization in systems from swarms of insects to superconductors. We have recently found a connection between the original, real-valued nonlinear Kuramoto model and a corresponding complex-valued system that permits describing the system in terms of a linear operator and iterative update rule.

arxiv-2210-10437.title: Nonreciprocal Charge Transport in Topological Kagome Superconductor CsV 3 Sb 5
arxiv-2210-10437.creator: Yueshen Wu, Qi Wang, Xiang Zhou, Jinghui Wang, Peng Dong, Jiadian He, Yifan Ding, Bolun Teng, Yiwen Zhang, Yifei Li, Chenglong Zhao, Hongti Zhang, Jianpeng Liu, Yanpeng Qi, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Jun Li
arxiv-2210-10437.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yueshen Wu, Qi Wang, Xiang Zhou, Jinghui Wang, Peng Dong, Jiadian He, Yifan Ding, Bolun Teng, Yiwen Zhang, Yifei Li, Chenglong Zhao, Hongti Zhang, Jianpeng Liu, Yanpeng Qi, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Jun Li. Nonreciprocal charge transport phenomena are widely studied in two-dimensional superconductors, which demonstrate unidirectional-anisotropy magnetoresistances as a result of symmetry breaking. Here, we report a strong nonreciprocal transport phenomenon in superconducting CsV 3 Sb 5 thin flakes.

arxiv-2303-03119.title: Multiverse Predictions for Habitability: Stellar and Atmospheric Habitability
arxiv-2303-03119.creator: McCullen Sandora *, Vladimir Airapetian, Luke Barnes, Geraint F. Lewis
arxiv-2303-03119.description: Abstract Stellar activity and planetary atmospheric properties have the potential to strongly influence habitability. To date, neither have been adequately studied in the multiverse context, so there has been no assessment of how these effects impact the probabilities of observing our fundamental constants.

arxiv-2501-06839.title: Capability of anti-degradable quantum channel with additional entanglement
arxiv-2501-06839.creator: Changchun Zhong
arxiv-2501-06839.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Changchun Zhong. Quantum communication theory focuses on the study of quantum channels for transmitting quantum information, where the transmission rate is measured by quantum channel capacity. This quantity exhibits several intriguing properties, such as non-additivity, superactivation and so on. In this work, we show that a type of quantum channel known as the anti-degradable one-mode Gaussian channel—whose capacity is believed to be zero—can be “activated” to transmit quantum information through the introduction of quantum entanglement.

arxiv-2511-12288.creator: Yihan Dai, Sijie Liang, Haotian Xu, Peichu Xie, Sergey Mechtaev
arxiv-2511-12288.description: Abstract . When generating code from natural language prompts, an LLM samples programs from a probability distribution, many of which might be incorrect. Sample consensus techniques — such as majority voting or validation against generated tests or specifications — aim to identify a correct program in the sample or abstain if none is valid.

arxiv-2601-09253.title: RIFT: Repurposing Negative Samples via Reward-Informed Fine-Tuning
arxiv-2601-09253.creator: Zehua Liu, Shuqi Liu, Tao Zhong, Mingxuan YuanHuawei Noah’s Ark Lab liuzehua@connect.hku.hk, liu.shuqi1@huawei.com
arxiv-2601-09253.description: Abstract While Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Rejection Sampling Fine-Tuning (RFT) are standard for LLM alignment, they either rely on costly expert data or discard valuable negative samples, leading to data inefficiency. To address this, we propose Reward Informed Fine-Tuning (RIFT), a simple yet effective framework that utilizes all self-generated samples.

pmc-11437265.title: A novel computational signal processing framework towards multimodal vital signs extraction using neck-worn wearable devices
pmc-11437265.creator: Rawan S. Abdulsadig, Esther Rodriguez-Villegas
pmc-11437265.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Pulse rate (PR) and respiratory rate (RR) are two of the most important vital signs. Monitoring them would benefit from easy-to-use technologies. Hence, wearable devices would, in principle, be ideal candidates for such systems. The neck, although highly susceptible to artifacts, presents an attractive location for a diverse pool of physiological biomarkers monitoring purposes such as airflow sensing in a non-obstructive manner.

pmc-11478325.title: Optical Properties and Applications of Diffraction Grating Using Localized Surface Plasmon Resonance with Metal Nano-Hemispheres
pmc-11478325.creator: Tomoya Kubota, Shogo Tokimori, Kai Funato, Hiroaki Kawata, Tetsuya Matsuyama, Kenji Wada, Koichi Okamoto, Carlo Altucci
pmc-11478325.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). This study investigates the optical properties of diffraction gratings using localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) with metal nano-hemispheres. We fabricated metal nano-hemisphere gratings (MNHGS) with Ga, Ag, and Au and examined their wavelength-selective diffraction properties. Our findings show that these gratings exhibit peak diffraction efficiencies at 300 nm, 500 nm, and 570 nm, respectively, corresponding to the LSPR wavelengths of each metal. The MNHGs were created through thermal nanoimprint and metal deposition, followed by annealing.

pmc-11599077.title: EMSIG: Uncovering Factors Influencing COVID-19 Vaccination Across Different Subgroups Characterized by Embedding-Based Spatial Information Gain
pmc-11599077.creator: Zongliang Yue, Nicholas P McCormick, Oluchukwu M Ezeala, Spencer H Durham, Salisa C Westrick, Alessandra Casuccio
pmc-11599077.description: Background/Objectives: COVID-19 and its variants continue to pose significant threats to public health, with considerable uncertainty surrounding their impact. As of September 2024, the total number of deaths reached 8.8 million worldwide. Vaccination remains the most effective strategy for preventing COVID-19. However, vaccination rates in the Deep South, U.S., are notably lower than the national average due to various factors.

pmc-11720615.title: Differential expression of ABO in normal and tumor tissues: Implications for cancer biology and prognosis
pmc-11720615.creator: Hind M. Albadrani, Munerah Hamed, Abeer Zakariyah, Samar Binkheder, Saeed M. Kabrah, Arwa F. Flemban
pmc-11720615.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ObjectivesABO, which is primarily recognized for determining blood types, shows variable expression patterns in different tissues and cancer types. This study investigated the relationship between gene expression and cancer, and assessed its potential impact on patient survival.MethodsUtilizing the GEPIA database, we analyzed ABO expression in normal and tumor tissues across various cancer types using online in silico tools for comprehensive evaluation.ResultsThe analysis revealed significant disparities in ABO expression among different tissue types.

pmc-12800978.title: Patient-Specific 3-Dimensional Surgical Guide for Anteriorizing Tibial Tubercle Osteotomy to Treat Patellofemoral Osteoarthritis
pmc-12800978.creator: Ashton Kai Shun Tan, Shaun Kai Kiat Chua, Don Thong Siang Koh, Junwei Soong, Hamid Rahmatullah Bin Abd Razak, Shing Yi Tan, Kong Hwee Lee
pmc-12800978.description: There is an emerging role of using patient-specific instruments in orthopaedic surgery, such as high tibial osteotomy, to improve surgical precision and reduce operative times. However, there is a paucity of evidence in the use of patient-specific instruments in anteriorizing tibial tubercle osteotomy (aTTO) to treat patellofemoral osteoarthritis.

pmc-13064270.title: Alpha-1 antitrypsin–glucocorticoid receptor axis: a new pathway in immune modulation
pmc-13064270.creator: Kevin Möhlis, Julia Held, Elena Korenbaum, Sabine Wrenger, Sabina Janciauskiene, John T. Heiker
pmc-13064270.description: BackgroundAlpha-1 antitrypsin (AAT) has been reported to interact with the glucocorticoid receptor (GR) and modulate its signaling. We extended these findings by testing whether native (nAAT) and oxidized AAT (oxAAT) bind GR.MethodsBinding of native and modified AAT (oxidized and cleaved) to GR and candidate receptors (LRP1, SR-B1, TfR, CD36) was assessed by ELISA.

pmc-13248519.title: Safety evaluation of an extension of use of the food enzyme glucan 1,4‐α‐maltohydrolase from the genetically modified Bacillus licheniformis strain NZYM‐FR
pmc-13248519.creator: EFSA Panel on Food Enzymes (FEZ), Holger Zorn, José Manuel Barat Baviera, Claudia Bolognesi, Francesco Catania, Gabriele Gadermaier, Ralf Greiner, Baltasar Mayo, Alicja Mortensen, Yrjö Henrik Roos, Marize L M Solano, Henk Van Loveren, Laurence Vernis, Irene Bonino, Daniele Cavanna, Yi Liu
pmc-13248519.description: The food enzyme glucan 1,4‐α‐maltohydrolase (4‐α‐d‐glucan α‐maltohydrolase, EC 3.2.1.133) is produced with the genetically modified Bacillus licheniformis strain NZYM‐FR by Novozymes A/S. The safety of this food enzyme was evaluated previously and it did not give rise to safety concerns when used in three food manufacturing processes.

pmc-13320091.title: The exploitation argument against artificial companionship
pmc-13320091.creator: Jonathon VandenHombergh
pmc-13320091.description: There is increasing interest in the use of artificial intelligence for companionship. Most resistance to this proposal appeals to the risk of deception: the idea that, because they lack the relevant mental states, artificial companions cannot authentically befriend their users.

pmc-13386774.title: Fine-tuning sequence-to-expression models on personal genome and transcriptome data
pmc-13386774.creator: Ruchir Rastogi, Aniketh Janardhan Reddy, Ryan Chung, Nilah M. Ioannidis
pmc-13386774.description: BackgroundGenomic sequence-to-expression deep learning models, which are trained to predict gene expression and other molecular phenotypes across the reference genome, have recently been shown to have poor out-of-the-box performance in predicting gene expression variation across individuals based on their personal genome sequences.

pmc-13553532.title: Association of caffeine citrate plus vitamin A/D drops with bronchopulmonary dysplasia and respiratory outcomes in preterm infants born at <32 weeks’ gestation: a 72-h landmark retrospective cohort study
pmc-13553532.creator: Rongying Su, Yaohua Pei
pmc-13553532.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveThe aim of this work is to examine whether the early addition of vitamin A/D drops to caffeine citrate was associated with bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) and short-term respiratory outcomes in preterm infants born at <32 weeks’ gestation.MethodsThis single-center, 72-h landmark retrospective cohort study included 126 infants admitted to the hospital between October 2022 and November 2024 with a gestational age <32 weeks and birth weight ≤1.5 kg.

pmc-13627440.title: A novel stop-loss variant in ISG15 causes C-terminal dysfunction and impairs USP18-mediated negative feedback
pmc-13627440.creator: Wanyu Zhang, Xiongbin Chen, Yulu Li, Xingfeng Yao, Jinyan Huang, Yijiu Gao, Wenlu Xing, Dan Lu, Mengyue Deng, Zhou Shu, Huawei Mao
pmc-13627440.description: IntroductionISG15 is a type I interferon (IFN-I)-inducible ubiquitin-like protein that restrains IFN-I signaling. Classical ISG15 deficiency is thought to cause disease mainly by disrupting USP18 stabilization, which leads to sustained IFN-I signaling and interferon-driven autoinflammation. Whether patient-derived C-terminal ISG15 variants can impair IFN-I negative feedback through altered C-terminal functional presentation has remained unclear.

uslaw-usc-t5-s594.title: 5 U.S.C. § 594 — Powers and duties of the Conference
uslaw-usc-t5-s594.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t5-s594.description: United States Code, Title 5 (Government Organization And Employees); Part I (The Agencies Generally); Chapter 5 (Administrative Procedure); Subchapter V (Administrative Conference Of The United States). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. To carry out the purposes of this subchapter, the Administrative Conference of the United States may— (1) study the efficiency, adequacy, and fairness of the administrative procedure used by administrative agencies.
